issue.title: gh secret set --body - stores literal "-" instead of reading stdin
issue.body:
## Bug: `gh secret set --body -` stores the literal string `-` instead of reading stdin

### Expected
`echo "s3cret" | gh secret set MYSECRET --body -` should store `s3cret`, following the universal `-` = stdin convention (which `gh secret set --env-file -` already honors in the same command).

### Actual
The secret is set to the literal one-character string `-`. Stdin is silently ignored. No error, no warning.

### Why this happens
In `pkg/cmd/secret/set/set.go`, `getBody()` returns `[]byte(opts.Body)` verbatim for any non-empty `--body`, with no `-` special-casing — while `--env-file` explicitly checks `opts.EnvFile == "-"` and reads stdin. Same command, adjacent flags, inconsistent behavior.

### Impact
This is a silent data-corruption footgun: the command succeeds, so automation (e.g. `spawnSync("gh", ["secret", "set", ..., "--body", "-"], {input: token})`) believes the real secret was stored while GitHub holds `-`. I lost an hour to this provisioning a CI credential before reading the source.

### Proposed fix
Treat `--body -` like an absent `--body` so it falls through to the stdin read in `getBody()`. Happy to open the PR.
